memories.content: The user's maternal aunt keeps one spare key to the user's home.
If the door is locked, the user is accustomed to contacting their maternal aunt, who has the spare key, before contacting building management.
When going to collect the spare key from their maternal aunt, the user wants to give an arrival time first so neither person has to wait.
The user feels at ease only after returning a borrowed spare key in person on the same day.
The user feels uneasy about writing down a new entrance passcode on paper.
The user found it difficult when a family member arrived without notice during a meeting and the user could not respond immediately.
On a day their younger brother received a package for them, the user felt reassured after checking the delivery photo.
The user's maternal aunt wants confirmation that the user is coming in person before handing over the spare key.
Confirm with the user before sharing the spare key's storage location or the maternal aunt's contact information.
The management office of a multi-unit residential building does not hold a unit key without verifying identity.
The user keeps the book they are reading and a note-taking notebook on a small living-room desk.
While reading in the living room with the television on, the user read the same paragraph three times.
The next day, after turning off the television, the user read 40 pages without interruption.
On a day the phone was on the desk, the user stopped taking notes each time they checked a notification.
During the next reading period, the user left the phone in another room and did not check it for an hour.
A note attached to a paper book fell out, and the user had to find their place again.
With the next book, the user recorded the page number in the notebook and resumed reading immediately.
The user's father expects that lowering the television volume while the user reads will make it easier for the user to concentrate.
The local agent can summarize past reading environments and interruption records but cannot predict the next reading time.
The user feels that repeated notifications interrupt their flow of concentration.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: the reference frame concerns home access, family coordination, privacy, and delivery reassurance, while the compared frame concerns reading environments, interruption control, place-keeping, and agent limits. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.
